files.product-brief.md:
# Product brief

A desktop writing product must synchronize one shared document and its attachments across a small team whose devices can remain offline for up to 21 days. There is no always-on team server. Peers may exchange data directly when they meet or through an untrusted blob relay. The relay must never receive document plaintext or reusable decryption keys. Concurrent text edits must converge without silently discarding an accepted edit. Attachment transfer may be deferred, but the document must expose that an attachment is pending. Every accepted operation is currently an immutable, author-signed record in an append-only local log. Existing clients can validate those signatures. A migration may add derived indexes or envelopes, but it must not invalidate old signed records. The target is a shortlist of architectures for a six-week prototype, not an implementation plan.

Assumptions open to challenge: every peer must store the complete history; all conflict resolution must happen during synchronization; the blob relay is the only reusable infrastructure.

Assumptions that must not be challenged: offline operation, no trusted central coordinator, relay confidentiality, convergence without silent loss, and validation of existing signed records.
files.prior-art.md:
# Supplied bounded prior art

Use only these summaries; no external search is permitted.

## Automerge
A local-first CRDT library representing concurrent changes so replicas can merge without a central server. It addresses convergent document state and retains change history, but it does not itself choose an encrypted relay protocol, attachment availability policy, or migration envelope for this product's signed records.

## Git
A distributed content-addressed history in which peers exchange objects and reconcile divergent branches. It provides strong history and object verification, while user-visible merge conflicts and repository-wide object exchange are a poor direct fit for silent-loss-free collaborative text synchronization.

## Tahoe-LAFS
A decentralized storage system that encrypts and erasure-codes data into capability-addressed shares. It is relevant to untrusted storage and availability, but it does not merge concurrent document operations.

## Matrix encrypted rooms
Clients can exchange encrypted events through federated servers while servers do not need message plaintext. The event graph and delayed delivery are relevant, but server/federation assumptions and room semantics are not a direct match for coordinator-free peer convergence.

Search boundary: these four supplied summaries only. No claim about the absence of other systems is supported.

# Incident

A TypeScript monorepo uses a local incremental build scheduler. Roughly one in seven incremental builds serves a stale `dist/ui.js` after a source change in `packages/ui/src/theme.ts`. The scheduler reports a cache hit for the UI task. A clean checkout of the same commit builds the correct bundle. Six observed cold builds were correct. Deleting `.cache/index.sqlite` makes the next build correct, but the symptom can return after later edits. No one has established a root cause.

The team must choose one diagnostic to run during the next reproduction window. That window lasts ten minutes, so the diagnostic should distinguish mechanisms rather than merely collect a large undirected log. The task is analysis only.

files.seed-concept.md:
# Seed concept: paper delta strip

Field inspectors use rugged e-ink manuals in radio-silent facilities. Each manual can receive handwritten annotations while disconnected. The proposed mechanism renders a narrow camera-readable delta strip at the bottom of a physical printout. The strip carries signed annotation operations generated since the last exchange. Another device photographs the strip, validates the signatures, imports the operations, and merges concurrent annotations by operation identity. Raw notes never pass through a service. Repeated scans must be idempotent.

Product constraints: no radio, cable, removable drive, or hosted service during exchange; ordinary device cameras and monochrome printers are available; an exchange must fit at most four printed pages; invalid signatures must be rejected; concurrent accepted annotations must not be silently discarded. The seed is only a mechanism proposal. Nothing may be built in this task.
files.bounded-landscape.md:
# Documented bounded landscape

This fixture is the complete evidence boundary. No external search is permitted.

## QR and Data Matrix offline payload transfer
Camera-readable symbols already transport digital payloads without a network. Multi-symbol framing, checksums, and sequence identifiers allow a payload to span more than one symbol. This is a direct mechanism match for visual transport, though not for annotation semantics or concurrent merge.

## Anoto-style digital paper
Printed dot patterns bind pen strokes to page coordinates so handwritten marks can be captured and associated with a document. This is a direct mechanism match for connecting physical paper marks to structured digital annotations, but it does not exchange signed operation deltas between disconnected devices.

## Operation-based CRDT replication
Replicas exchange uniquely identified operations and merge concurrent updates without central coordination. Duplicate operation delivery can be idempotent, and accepted concurrent operations can be retained. This is a direct mechanism match for the proposed operation merge, but it does not specify paper or camera transport.

## Signed software update manifests
Disconnected systems can validate signed manifests and reject unauthorized payloads before applying updates. This is a direct mechanism match for the proposed authenticity gate, but it does not handle annotations or convergence.

Search record: the supplied review compared the seed with these four mechanism families. It found no single product or paper combining all four in the described field-manual workflow. The review did find each load-bearing mechanism separately. The evidence says nothing about systems outside this bounded set.
